question: You put a Button on a screen and set it up. Should you be able to point it at a different component without starting over?
context: A copy of a component follows an original: change the original and every copy follows. Today a copy is stuck following the one it was made from. Choosing a different one means deleting it and placing the other, then setting its size, its room and its knobs again by hand.

options.label: A row in the panel that says which one it is
options.summary: Pick the copy and the panel shows the component it follows, as a row you can click to choose another. Choosing one keeps where it sits, how big it is, and every setting the new one also has.
pros: The panel already says which component a copy follows, so this is that line becoming something you can use
You can see what it is before you change it
Reads the same whether the copy is on its own, inside a group, or inside another component
cons: It is one more row in a panel that is already full
options.mitigation: It replaces the line that is there rather than adding one.

options.label: Drop the new one on top of the old one
options.summary: Drag a tile out of the Library and let it go on top of a copy that is already there, and it takes that copy over: same place, same size, same settings where they fit.
pros: Nothing new on screen at all
The gesture you already use to place one is the gesture that swaps one
cons: Easy to do by accident when you meant to put a second one next to the first
Nothing on screen tells you it is possible
options.mitigation: The copy underneath lights up while you hover it, and letting go anywhere else places a new one as it does today.

options.label: Both, the row and the drop
options.summary: The panel row is how you find out you can do it, and dropping one on top is the fast way once you know.
pros: Each one covers the other´s weakness
cons: Two ways into the same thing is two things to keep agreeing with each other
More to build and more to get wrong
options.mitigation: Build the row first and add the drop after, so the second one is judged against a working first.

options.label: Leave it: delete it and place the other one
options.summary: Changing your mind about which component a copy is means deleting it and dragging out the other, setting it up again.
pros: Nothing new to learn and nothing new to get wrong
One less thing in the panel
cons: Every setting you had made is lost and retyped
On a screen with twenty copies, trying a different button means twenty deletions
options.mitigation: None. This is the answer that says the app is for building screens once rather than exploring them.
